mock_data.title: Burning Issue
mock_data.passage:
A New Scientist comment article by Bethan Ackerley about the need for a climate change TV drama as impactful as Adolescence.

Everyone in the UK is talking about Adolescence. Created by Jack Thorne and Stephen Graham, the hit TV drama follows the investigation into a 13-year-old boy accused of killing a female classmate. It has sparked conversations about social media and the so-called manosphere, an online community of misogynistic influencers.

It has been so widely praised that UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer recently met the team behind Adolescence to discuss the online radicalisation of teenage boys. Meanwhile, the leader of the UK's Conservative party, Kemi Badenoch, endured a minor media firestorm after revealing she hadn't seen the series.

I am not here to give my view on whether plans to show Adolescence in UK schools will lessen misogyny among children. But what it did make me wonder is which other TV series our political leaders should be watching – and why the most pressing crisis of our times is yet to receive the Adolescence treatment.

Television, perhaps more than any other medium, is seen as a vehicle for change. Thorne has called it the "empathy box": it lives in our homes, evolving alongside us and making us better people.

Sometimes, it really does work like that. The 1960s drama Cathy Come Home led to the creation of homelessness charity Crisis, while a 2018 survey found that women in the US who regularly watched The X-Files were more likely to believe that women should study STEM subjects. And the 2024 drama Mr Bates vs The Post Office – about the hundreds of UK Post Office employees wrongly prosecuted due to a faulty IT system – led to more than 100 new potential victims seeking legal advice.

But one issue where this hasn't happened is climate change. While documentaries have long played their part in informing the public about ecological crises, they don't seem to be enough. Take the 2017 series Blue Planet II. This is widely credited with raising awareness of marine plastic pollution, yet there is little evidence it caused enduring changes to consumer habits.

So could television really help save our planet? Fiction, not fact, may be key. We know storytelling is a prosocial behaviour and that acting for the collective good is vital for passing climate legislation. Heavy viewers of fictional TV have also been shown to more strongly believe in justice than do viewers of news and documentaries, which could prove crucial in stopping climate nihilism from taking hold.

We also know that awe – which encourages individuals to see themselves as small elements of a far larger world – is a powerful tool for preventing climate inaction. Science fiction may therefore be uniquely helpful: last year, researchers found that sci-fi was distinct in its ability to inspire awe and was linked to people identifying with all humanity. Even the act of imagining the future might encourage leaders to look beyond the next election and take long-term action.

What we need, then, is an Adolescence for climate change. If I could choose an existing series for politicians to watch, I would pick the 2019 drama Years and Years, which followed a British family living through the rise of fascism as the planet burns. For All Mankind – an alternate history of the space race, in which greater investment in new technologies slows down global warming – might also prove inspirational.

But some yet-to-be-adapted sci-fi novels would be even better. Who could watch a small-screen version of Octavia E. Butler's Parable of the Sower, Ursula K. Le Guin's The Word for World Is Forest or Kim Stanley Robinson's The Ministry for the Future and not be inspired to save our precious home planet? The opportunities are endless – we just need some fantastic writers to take them. Perhaps that could be Thorne and Graham's next project.
mock_data.passageB1:
A TV show called Adolescence is very popular in the UK. Bethan Ackerley, a writer for New Scientist, thinks we need a TV show about climate change that is just as good.

Adolescence is about a 13-year-old boy who is accused of hurting a girl at school. It was made by Jack Thorne and Stephen Graham. The show has made people talk about social media and some online groups that don't like women, called the manosphere.

Many people like the show. Even Keir Starmer, who is the leader of the UK, met with the people who made Adolescence. They talked about how young boys can be influenced online. Kemi Badenoch, another leader in the UK, got some negative attention because she said she hadn't watched the show.

I don't want to say if showing Adolescence in schools will help stop people from disliking women. But it made me think about what other TV shows leaders should watch. And why there isn't a TV show about the most important problem of our time: climate change.

TV can help to make a change. Jack Thorne says TV is like a box that helps us understand each other better. It's in our homes and changes with us, and it can make us better people.

Sometimes, this is true. A TV show from the 1960s called Cathy Come Home helped start a charity for homeless people. And a study in 2018 found that women in the US who watched The X-Files thought that women should study science more. In 2024, a TV show called Mr Bates vs The Post Office showed how many UK Post Office workers were wrongly accused of crimes because of a computer problem. After the show, more than 100 people asked for legal help.

But there isn't a good TV show that has helped with climate change. Documentaries have told people about the problems with the environment, but they don't seem to be enough. For example, the TV show Blue Planet II in 2017 made people more aware of plastic pollution in the ocean. But it didn't really change how people used things.

So, can TV really help to save the planet? Maybe a story, not just facts, is the answer. We know that telling stories is good for people, and that working together is important for passing laws about climate change. People who watch a lot of TV shows also believe more strongly in justice than people who watch the news. This could help stop people from giving up on climate change.

We also know that feeling amazement can help. It makes people feel like they are a small part of a big world. This can stop people from not doing anything about climate change. Science fiction might be very helpful. Last year, researchers found that science fiction can make people feel amazement and can make them feel like they are connected to everyone in the world. Even just imagining the future might make leaders think about more than just the next election and take action for the long term.

So, we need a TV show about climate change that is as good as Adolescence. If I could choose a TV show for politicians to watch, I would choose Years and Years from 2019. It's about a British family living through a time when bad people are in power and the planet is burning. For All Mankind is another good show. It shows a different history of the space race, where new technologies helped to slow down global warming.

But some science fiction books that haven't been made into TV shows yet would be even better. If people watched a TV show based on Octavia E. Butler's Parable of the Sower, Ursula K. Le Guin's The Word for World Is Forest, or Kim Stanley Robinson's The Ministry for the Future, they would want to save the planet. There are many opportunities. We just need some great writers to make them happen. Maybe Jack Thorne and Stephen Graham could do it next.

mock_data.passageC1:
The overwhelming public discourse in the UK currently revolves around 'Adolescence', Jack Thorne and Stephen Graham's critically acclaimed television drama. This series, which meticulously dissects the investigation into a 13-year-old accused of murdering a classmate, has galvanized conversations surrounding the pervasive influence of social media and the so-called 'manosphere' – a digital ecosystem teeming with misogynistic content creators.

Such has been its impact that Prime Minister Keir Starmer recently convened with the creative minds behind 'Adolescence' to deliberate on strategies for counteracting the online radicalisation of young males. Conversely, Kemi Badenoch, a prominent figure within the Conservative party, found herself embroiled in a minor media controversy after admitting her unfamiliarity with the series.

My intention here isn't to weigh in on the merits of incorporating 'Adolescence' into the UK school curriculum as a potential remedy for misogyny. Rather, its success begs the question: what other pressing societal issues warrant similar treatment on screen, and why hasn't the climate crisis – arguably the defining challenge of our era – received its 'Adolescence' moment?

Television, perhaps more than any other medium, is widely perceived as a potent catalyst for social change. Thorne himself aptly describes it as the 'empathy box', insinuating its capacity to reside within our homes, evolve in tandem with our values, and ultimately, foster a more enlightened society.

History bears witness to instances where this potential has been realised. The seminal 1960s drama 'Cathy Come Home' served as the impetus for the establishment of Crisis, a prominent homelessness charity. Moreover, a 2018 survey revealed a correlation between consistent viewership of 'The X-Files' among women in the US and a stronger conviction that women should pursue careers in STEM fields. Most recently, the 2024 drama 'Mr Bates vs The Post Office', chronicling the wrongful prosecution of hundreds of UK Post Office employees due to a flawed IT system, prompted over 100 additional potential victims to seek legal recourse.

However, the same cannot be said for climate change. While documentaries have undoubtedly played a crucial role in disseminating information about ecological crises, their impact appears to be insufficient to induce meaningful behavioural shifts. For instance, the 2017 series 'Blue Planet II' is widely credited with raising awareness of marine plastic pollution, yet concrete evidence of enduring changes in consumer habits remains elusive.

Therefore, the question arises: could television, specifically fictional narratives, genuinely contribute to safeguarding our planet? Storytelling, as a fundamentally prosocial behaviour, may hold the key. Collective action, driven by a sense of shared responsibility, is indispensable for enacting effective climate legislation. Research also suggests that avid consumers of fictional television are more likely to harbour a strong belief in justice than those who primarily consume news and documentaries, which could prove vital in preventing the proliferation of climate nihilism.

Furthermore, the cultivation of awe – a sentiment that encourages individuals to perceive themselves as integral yet diminutive components of a vast, interconnected world – represents a powerful tool for combating climate inaction. Science fiction, with its capacity to transport viewers to alternative realities and explore the far-reaching consequences of our actions, may be particularly effective in this regard. Last year, studies indicated that sci-fi possesses a unique ability to inspire awe and foster a sense of shared humanity. Even the act of envisioning potential future scenarios might incentivise leaders to transcend the short-term focus of electoral cycles and embrace long-term, sustainable strategies.

What we urgently require, then, is a climate change equivalent of 'Adolescence'. Were I tasked with selecting an existing series for politicians to watch, I would undoubtedly recommend the 2019 drama 'Years and Years', which poignantly portrays a British family navigating the rise of fascism against the backdrop of a planet ravaged by environmental degradation. 'For All Mankind', an alternate history of the space race where increased investment in innovative technologies mitigates global warming, might also serve as a source of inspiration.

However, certain unadapted science fiction novels possess even greater potential to exert influence. Who could remain unmoved by a small-screen adaptation of Octavia E. Butler's 'Parable of the Sower', Ursula K. Le Guin's 'The Word for World Is Forest', or Kim Stanley Robinson's 'The Ministry for the Future'? The possibilities are boundless; all that remains is for gifted writers to seize the initiative. Perhaps Thorne and Graham might consider this as their next compelling project, thereby amplifying the urgency of climate action and fostering a groundswell of support for meaningful change. It is a challenge that demands immediate attention, lest we allow apathy and inaction to seal our fate.

mock_data.translation:
Bethan Ackerley tomonidan yozilgan New Scientist sharh maqolasi — Adolescence singari ta'sirchan iqlim o'zgarishi TV dramasi zaruriyati haqida.

Buyuk Britaniyada hamma Adolescence haqida gapirmoqda. Jek Torn va Stiven Grem tomonidan yaratilgan mashhur teleserial sinfdosh qizni o'ldirganlikda ayblanayotgan 13 yoshli bolaga nisbatan tergovni kuzatadi. Bu ijtimoiy tarmoqlar va ayollarga nisbatan nafrat uyg'otuvchi ta'sirchilarning onlayn jamoasi bo'lgan "manosphere" haqida suhbatlarni qo'zg'adi.

U shunchalik keng maqtalganki, Buyuk Britaniya Bosh vaziri Keir Starmer yaqinda o'smir bolalarning onlayn radikallashishi haqida gaplashish uchun Adolescence jamoasi bilan uchrashdi. Shu bilan birga, Buyuk Britaniya Konservativ partiyasi rahbari Kemi Badenoch serialni ko'rmaganligini aytgandan keyin kichik media bo'roniga duch keldi.

Men Adolescenceni Buyuk Britaniya maktablarida ko'rsatish rejalari bolalar orasida ayollarga nafratni kamaytiradimi yoki yo'qmi haqida fikr bildirish uchun bu yerda emasman. Lekin bu meni qiziqtirgan narsa — siyosiy rahbarlarimiz yana qaysi seriallarni tomosha qilishlari kerak va nima uchun zamonimizning eng dolzarb inqirozi hali Adolescence muomalasini olmagan.

Televizion, boshqa har qanday vositadan ko'ra ko'proq, o'zgarishlar uchun vosita sifatida qaraladi. Torn uni "hamdardlik qutisi" deb atagan: u bizning uylarimizda yashaydi, biz bilan birga rivojlanadi va bizni yaxshiroq odamlar qiladi.

Ba'zan bu chindan ham shunday ishlaydi. 1960-yillardagi Cathy Come Home dramasi uysizlar xayriya tashkiloti Crisis tashkil etilishiga olib keldi, 2018-yilgi so'rov esa AQShda The X-Filesni muntazam tomosha qiladigan ayollar STEM fanlarini o'qishi kerak deb ko'proq ishonishini aniqladi. Va 2024-yildagi Mr Bates vs The Post Office dramasi – noto'g'ri IT tizimi tufayli noto'g'ri jinoiy javobgarlikka tortilgan yuzlab Buyuk Britaniya pochta xodimlari haqida – 100 dan ortiq yangi potentsial jabrlanuvchilarning huquqiy maslahat so'rashiga olib keldi.

Ammo bu sodir bo'lmagan bir masala – iqlim o'zgarishi. Hujjatli filmlar uzoq vaqtdan beri ekologik inqirozlar haqida jamoatchilikni xabardor qilishda o'z rolini o'ynagan bo'lsa-da, ular yetarli bo'lmayotganga o'xshaydi. 2017-yilgi Blue Planet II serialini olaylik. Bu dengiz plastik ifloslanishi haqida xabardorlikni oshirganlik bilan keng tan olingan, ammo u iste'mol odatlarida uzoq muddatli o'zgarishlarga sabab bo'lganligi haqida kam dalil bor.

Xo'sh, televizion haqiqatan ham sayyoramizni qutqara oladimi? Haqiqat emas, badiiy asar kalit bo'lishi mumkin. Biz hikoya qilish ijtimoiy foydali xulq-atvor ekanligini va jamoaviy manfaat uchun harakat qilish iqlim qonunchiligi qabul qilish uchun muhim ekanligini bilamiz. Badiiy televizionning faol tomoshabinlari yangiliklar va hujjatli filmlar tomoshabinlariga qaraganda adolatga ko'proq ishonishi ham ko'rsatilgan, bu iqlim nigilizmining kuchayishini to'xtatishda hal qiluvchi ahamiyatga ega bo'lishi mumkin.

Biz shuningdek, hayrat – odamlarni o'zlarini ancha kattaroq dunyoning kichik elementlari sifatida ko'rishga undaydigan – iqlim harakatsizligini oldini olish uchun kuchli vosita ekanligini bilamiz. Ilmiy fantastika shuning uchun noyob darajada foydali bo'lishi mumkin: o'tgan yili tadqiqotchilar ilmiy fantastikaning hayrat uyg'otish qobiliyatida o'ziga xos ekanligini va butun insoniyat bilan o'zini bir tutish bilan bog'liqligini aniqladilar. Hatto kelajakni tasavvur qilish harakati rahbarlarni keyingi saylovdan nariroq qarashga va uzoq muddatli harakat qilishga undashi mumkin.

Bizga kerak bo'lgan narsa — iqlim o'zgarishi uchun Adolescence. Agar men siyosatchilar tomosha qilishi uchun mavjud serialni tanlashim mumkin bo'lsa, 2019-yilgi Years and Years dramasini tanlardim, bu Britaniya oilasining sayyora yonayotganda fashizm ko'tarilishi davrida hayotini kuzatgan. For All Mankind – kosmik poyganing muqobil tarixi, unda yangi texnologiyalarga ko'proq sarmoya global isishni sekinlashtiradi – ham ilhomlantiruvchi bo'lishi mumkin.

Ammo hali moslashtirilmagan ba'zi ilmiy fantastik romanlar yanada yaxshiroq bo'lardi. Kim Oktaviya E. Batlerning Parable of the Sower, Ursula K. Le Guinning The Word for World Is Forest yoki Kim Stenli Robinsonning The Ministry for the Future asarining kichik ekran versiyasini tomosha qilib, qadrli uy sayyoramizni qutqarishga ilhomlanmasligi mumkin? Imkoniyatlar cheksiz – bizga faqat ajoyib yozuvchilar kerak. Ehtimol, bu Torn va Gremning keyingi loyihasi bo'lishi mumkin.

Buyuk Britaniyada "O'spirinlik" deb nomlangan teleserial juda mashhur. "New Scientist" jurnalining yozuvchisi Betan Ackerleyning fikricha, bizga xuddi shunday yaxshi iqlim o'zgarishi haqidagi teleserial ham kerak.

"O'spirinlik" 13 yoshli o'g'il bolaning maktabda bir qizni xafa qilganlikda ayblanishi haqida. Uni Jek Torn va Stiven Grem suratga olishgan. Serial odamlarni ijtimoiy tarmoqlar va ayollarni yoqtirmaydigan ba'zi onlayn guruhlar, manosfera haqida gapirishga majbur qildi.

Ko'pchilik serialni yaxshi ko'radi. Hatto Buyuk Britaniya rahbari Kir Starmer ham "O'spirinlik" filmini suratga olganlar bilan uchrashdi. Ular yosh o'g'il bolalarga onlayn ta'sir qanday bo'lishi mumkinligi haqida gaplashdilar. Buyuk Britaniyaning yana bir rahbari Kemi Badenoch serialni tomosha qilmaganini aytgani uchun salbiy e'tiborni tortdi.

Men "O'spirinlik"ni maktablarda ko'rsatish odamlarning ayollarga nisbatan nafratini to'xtatishga yordam beradimi yoki yo'qmi, aytmoqchi emasman. Lekin bu meni rahbarlar qanday teleseriallarni tomosha qilishlari kerakligi haqida o'ylashga majbur qildi. Va nima uchun bizning davrimizning eng muhim muammosi: iqlim o'zgarishi haqida teleserial yo'q.

Televideniye o'zgarish qilishga yordam berishi mumkin. Jek Torning aytishicha, televideniye bir-birimizni yaxshiroq tushunishga yordam beradigan qutiga o'xshaydi. U bizning uylarimizda va biz bilan birga o'zgaradi va bizni yaxshiroq odamlarga aylantirishi mumkin.

Ba'zan bu to'g'ri. 1960-yillardagi "Cathy Come Home" nomli teleserial uysiz odamlar uchun xayriya tashkilotini ochishga yordam berdi. 2018-yilda o'tkazilgan tadqiqot shuni ko'rsatdiki, AQShda "The X-Files"ni tomosha qilgan ayollar ayollar fanni ko'proq o'rganishlari kerak deb o'ylashgan. 2024-yilda "Mr Bates vs The Post Office" nomli teleserial Buyuk Britaniya pochta xodimlarining qancha qismi kompyuter muammosi tufayli nohaq jinoyatlarda ayblanganini ko'rsatdi. Serialdan so'ng 100 dan ortiq odam huquqiy yordam so'radi.

Ammo iqlim o'zgarishi bilan bog'liq vaziyatga yordam bergan yaxshi teleserial yo'q. Hujjatli filmlar odamlarga atrof-muhit bilan bog'liq muammolar haqida gapirib berdi, lekin ular yetarli emasdek tuyuladi. Masalan, 2017-yilda "Blue Planet II" teleseriali odamlarni okeandagi plastik ifloslanishi haqida ko'proq xabardor qildi. Ammo bu odamlarning narsalardan qanday foydalanishini unchalik o'zgartirmadi.

Xo'sh, televideniye sayyorani saqlashga haqiqatan ham yordam bera oladimi? Ehtimol, shunchaki faktlar emas, balki hikoya javob bo'lishi mumkin. Biz hikoya aytib berish odamlar uchun yaxshi ekanligini va iqlim o'zgarishi haqida qonunlar qabul qilish uchun birgalikda ishlash muhimligini bilamiz. Ko'p teleserial tomosha qiladigan odamlar yangiliklarni tomosha qiladigan odamlarga qaraganda adolatga ko'proq ishonishadi. Bu odamlarning iqlim o'zgarishidan voz kechishini to'xtatishga yordam berishi mumkin.

Shuningdek, biz hayratlanish hissi yordam berishi mumkinligini bilamiz. Bu odamlarni o'zlarini katta dunyoning kichik bir qismi kabi his qilishlariga olib keladi. Bu odamlarning iqlim o'zgarishi haqida hech narsa qilmasliklarini to'xtatishi mumkin. Ilmiy fantastika juda foydali bo'lishi mumkin. O'tgan yili tadqiqotchilar ilmiy fantastika odamlarda hayratlanish hissini uyg'otishi va ularni butun dunyodagi odamlar bilan bog'langanligini his qilishlariga olib kelishi mumkinligini aniqladilar. Hatto kelajakni tasavvur qilish ham rahbarlarni faqat keyingi saylov haqida o'ylashdan to'xtatib, uzoq muddatga chora ko'rishga undashi mumkin.

Shunday qilib, bizga "O'spirinlik" kabi yaxshi iqlim o'zgarishi haqidagi teleserial kerak. Agar men siyosatchilar uchun tomosha qilish uchun teleserialni tanlashim kerak bo'lsa, men 2019-yildagi "Years and Years"ni tanlagan bo'lardim. Unda yomon odamlar hokimiyatda bo'lgan va sayyora yonayotgan bir davrda yashayotgan britaniyalik oila haqida hikoya qilinadi. "For All Mankind" yana bir yaxshi serial. Unda kosmik poyganing boshqacha tarixi ko'rsatilgan, unda yangi texnologiyalar global isishni sekinlashtirishga yordam bergan.

Ammo hali teleserialga aylantirilmagan ba'zi ilmiy fantastika kitoblari undan ham yaxshiroq bo'lardi. Agar odamlar Oktaviya E. Batlerning "Parable of the Sower", Ursula K. Le Guinning "The Word for World Is Forest" yoki Kim Stenli Robinsonning "The Ministry for the Future" asarlari asosida suratga olingan teleserialni tomosha qilishsa, ular sayyorani saqlab qolishni xohlashadi. Imkoniyatlar ko'p. Bizga shunchaki ajoyib yozuvchilar kerak, ularni amalga oshirishlari kerak. Ehtimol, Jek Torn va Stiven Grem keyingi safar buni qilishlari mumkin.

Le Guinning "Dunyodagi o'rmon uchun so'z" yoki Kim Stenli Robinsonning "Kelajak uchun vazirlik" asarlarining kichik ekranli moslashuviga kim befarq qolishi mumkin? Imkoniyatlar cheksiz; qolganlari faqat iste'dodli yozuvchilarning tashabbusni qo'lga olishlaridir. Ehtimol, Torn va Grem buni o'zlarining keyingi qiziqarli loyihasi sifatida ko'rib chiqishlari mumkin, shu bilan iqlim harakatining dolzarbligini kuchaytirib va mazmunli o'zgarishlar uchun ommaviy qo'llab-quvvatlashni rag'batlantiradilar. Bu befarqlik va harakatsizlikka taqdirimizni hal qilishga yo'l qo'ymaslik uchun zudlik bilan e'tibor berishni talab qiladigan vazifadir.
